title: 678. Split Array into Consecutive Subsequences

examples.explanation: Groups [1,2,3] and [3,4,5] each run consecutively with length 3.
The leftover 4 and 5 cannot form a triple without breaking another group.

hints: Count occurrences of each value first.
Always try to extend an existing group waiting for the current value before starting a fresh triple.
Starting a new triple consumes one copy each of v, v+1 and v+2; fail when any is missing.
